# @ndigo/context

Application context, environments, configuration, and events for Ndigo

Version-matched export index for the installed package. Read `README.md`
for usage; the workspace guide index ships with `@ndigo/cli` as
`assets/agent/docs-index.md`.

## Public exports

- `ApplicationContext` *(type)* — Central application context: a hierarchical, configurable factory and event emitter.
- `ApplicationContextAware` *(type)* — Interface to be implemented by any object that wishes to be notified of the ApplicationContext that it runs in.
- `ConfigurableApplicationContext` *(type)* — Mutable application-context variant used during configuration.
- `LoggerAware` *(type)* — Interface to be implemented by any object that wishes to be notified of a Logger (typically obtained from the owning ApplicationContext) that it runs in.
- `likeApplicationContext` — Returns whether a value behaves like an application context.
- `likeApplicationContextAware` — Returns whether a value can receive an application context.
- `likeLoggerAware` — Returns whether a value behaves like a logger-aware object.
- `GenericApplicationContext` — Default application context implementation used throughout the package.
- `ProxiedGenericApplicationContext` — Application context proxy that exposes values as dynamic object properties.
- `AsApplicationContextAware`
- `AsLoggerAware` — Mixin adding logger awareness to a class.
- `ApplicationComponent` — Root of the component hierarchy: context-aware (`AsApplicationContextAware`) and otherwise empty, so `BusinessComponent` and `ViewComponent` share one ancestor…
- `BusinessComponent` — Base class for business logic components. Encapsulates domain rules and state orchestration.
- `ViewComponent` — Base class for view components. Encapsulates presentation logic and DOM interaction.
- `ApplicationContextAwareProcessor` — Create a new ApplicationContextAwareProcessor for the given context. An InitializationAwareProcessor implementation that passes the ApplicationContext to value…
- `ContextEvents` *(type)* — Application-context lifecycle events and their payloads.
- `EnvironmentEvents` *(type)* — Environment events and their payloads.
- `ShellContextOptions` *(type)* — Options for creating a shell context.
- `FeatureContextOptions` *(type)* — Options for creating a feature context and its optional relay gateway.
- `FeatureContextComposition` *(type)* — Result of mounting a feature context.
- `FeatureUnmountPolicy` *(type)* — Controls whether a feature context is closed or preserved during unmount.
- `createShellContext` — Create a shell/root context with optional infrastructure overrides.
- `createFeatureContext` — Create a feature context as a child of `parent`, optionally wiring an allowlisted relay gateway.
- `unmountFeatureContext` — Unmount a feature context by disconnecting relay gateway and optionally closing the context.

- `property` — Binds a class field to a property path resolved from the environment.

- `propertySource` — Adds a property source to a configuration class.
- `EntryDecorator` *(type)* — A method decorator that marks a configuration entry factory.
- `entry` — Creates an entry decorator from an explicit entry name (or context token).

- `MetadataConfigApplicationContext` — Application context that parses `@configuration` classes and registers their `@entry` values.
- `CONFIG_PROPS_PREFIX` — The `@configurationProperties` class prefix marker (`boot:configurationProperties:prefix`).
- `CONFIG_PROPS_RELAXED` — The relaxed-binding opt-in marker (`boot:configurationProperties:relaxed`).
- `CONFIG_PROPS_SCHEMA` — The schema-mode marker (`boot:configurationProperties:schema`, a zod type).
- `PROPERTY_KEY` — Field-level property metadata keys (set by the context decorators).
- `DEFAULT_KEY` — Metadata key for a field's default value.
- `NESTED_KEY` — Metadata key marking a nested configuration.
- `PROPERTY_KEY_TYPE` — Metadata key for a field's declared type.
- `getMetadata` — Reads configuration metadata from a class constructor.
- `DeclaredConfigurationProperty` *(type)* — A configuration property declared by a `@configurationProperties` class.
- `declaredConfigurationProperties` — Enumerate the configuration keys a `@configurationProperties` class declares, without resolving any value.
- `relaxedKeyCandidates` — The candidate environment keys `valueAt` probes for a dotted key under relaxed binding, exact key first, then its camelCase, kebab-case and snake_case spelling…

- `MockEnvironment`
- `StandardEnvironment` — Default environment implementation used by application contexts.
- `CONFIG_REFRESH_EVENT`
- `Environment` *(type)* — Resolves properties and manages profile activation for an application environment.
- `EnvironmentAware` *(type)* — Receives the current environment during initialization.
- `EnvironmentSource` *(type)* — Provides access to the environment associated with a component.
- `ConfigurableEnvironment` *(type)* — Environment variant that exposes its property registry and merge operations.
- `AbstractEnvironment` — Base implementation for environments with profile and property-source support.
- `AsEnvironmentAware`
- `likeEnvironment` — Tests whether a value behaves like an `Environment`.
- `likeEnvironmentAware` — Returns whether a value can receive an environment.
- `likeEnvironmentSource` — Returns whether a value exposes an environment.
- `EventListener` *(type)* — A listener callback for an emitted event.
- `EventHandler` *(type)* — A single listener or a listener list for an event type.
- `EventHandlers` *(type)* — Mapping from event type to handler(s).
- `EventType` *(type)* — Event type supported by the emitter.
- `EventEmitter` *(type)* — Emits and manages event listeners.
- `AsyncEventEmitter` *(type)* — Event emitter with microtask-based dispatch.
- `ConditionalEventEmitter` *(type)* — Event emitter with conditional and finite listeners.
- `PositionalEventEmitter` *(type)* — Event emitter that supports listener insertion positions.

- `AsPositionalEventEmitter` — Adds positional listener insertion helpers to a base class.
- `AsEventEmitter` — Adds the core event emitter API to a base class.
- `Emitter` — Standalone event emitter with destroy and serialization support.
- `EventEmitterTarget` *(type)* — Internal target shape used by the object mixin helper.
- `asEventEmitter` — Mixes event emitter behavior into an existing object.
- `ContextEventRelay` *(type)* — Maps an event emitted by the source context to a target event.

- `RelayValidationStrategy` *(type)* — Validates relay registrations before they are attached.
- `GatewayDiagnosticHandler` *(type)* — Receives relay registration and blocking diagnostics.
- `ContextEventGatewayOptions` *(type)* — Configures relay validation and diagnostics for a gateway.
- `NamespaceRelayValidationOptions` *(type)* — Options for namespace-based relay validation.
- `PermissiveRelayValidationStrategy` — Permissive relay validator that accepts all relays.
- `NamespaceRelayValidationStrategy` — Namespace-based relay validator for `site:*` and `<feature>:*` contracts.
- `InvalidRelayError` — Error thrown when a relay is rejected and throw-on-invalid mode is enabled.
- `ContextEventGateway` — Relays selected events from one application context to another.
- `FeatureMetricRecorder` *(type)*
- `LazyFeatureModule` *(type)* — A module loaded lazily by a feature's `loader`.

- `FeatureContextMountManager` — Creates, tracks, and tears down mounted feature contexts.

- `resolvePlaceholders` — Resolves `${key}` and `${key:default}` placeholders against a property resolver.

- `environment` — Marks a configuration class with the zod schema of its resolved environment — the schema IS the contract.
- `getEnvironmentSchema` — Returns the schema declared on a class via `@environment`, if any.
- `EnvironmentIssue` *(type)* — A single validation issue: the property path that failed, what was expected, and what the environment actually held.
- `ValidationResult` *(type)* — The structured result of validating an environment against a schema.
- `validateEnvironment` — Validates the resolved values of a property resolver against a zod schema.
- `PropertySource` *(type)* — A named, ordered property source backed by a plain object.
- `MapPropertySource` — Default PropertySource implementation wrapping a captured object.
- `wrapSource` — Creates a PropertySource that captures the given object.
- `PropertySources` *(type)* — Read-only view of the ordered, named PropertySource set.
- `MutablePropertySources` — Ordered, named property sources with O(1) name operations and keyed enumeration in precedence order (first = highest precedence).
- `SharedDependencyEntry` *(type)* — A single shared dependency entry.
- `DependencyValidationResult` *(type)* — Result of validating a feature's dependency manifest against the registry.
- `SharedDependencyRegistry` *(type)* — Registry that holds shared dependency declarations and validates feature manifests.
- `DefaultSharedDependencyRegistry` — Default implementation of `SharedDependencyRegistry`.
- `PropertyResolver` *(type)* — Resolves property values through an ordered source registry, with optional typed reads and secret decryption.
- `likePropertyResolver` — Returns whether a value behaves like a PropertyResolver.
- `PropertyIndex` *(type)* — Strategy interface for resolving property lookups from an ordered source list without walking the sources per lookup.
- `ResolverOptions` *(type)* — Options for constructing a property resolver / index-backed lookup.
- `PrototypeChainIndex` — Index that layers sources through a prototype chain.
- `FlatMergedIndex` — Index that merges sources into one flat object on build.
- `PrototypalPropertyResolver` — Property resolver that layers sources through a live property source registry.
- `REDACTED_VALUE` — The placeholder substituted for any value when a secret decryptor is configured — the value may be decrypted secret plaintext.
- `redactDiagnosticValue` — Formats a resolved property value for a diagnostic (error) message.
- `CONFIG_SERVER_SOURCE_NAME` — The default source name for the remote config source.

- `ConfigFileReader` *(type)* — Reads a file's text content, or `null` when the file does not exist.
